The Recreational Plateau: Why Traditional Coaching Often Falls Short

Most adult and competitive recreational players fall into a classic trap. They learn tennis later in life or develop ingrained muscle memory that contains minor flaws. When these players try to fix their strokes, they encounter three major roadblocks:

  • Information Overload: YouTube is flooded with thousands of conflicting tennis tips. One coach tells you to wipe windshield wipers on your forehand, while another emphasizes a completely different lag position. It leaves players confused and overthinking.
  • Focusing on Results Instead of Cause: Coaches often tell players what to do ("hit with more topspin") without teaching them how to coordinate their body segments to generate that topspin naturally.
  • The Expense of Private Coaching: High-level private tennis coaches are expensive—often charging anywhere from $70 to $150+ per hour. At that rate, fixing complex stroke flaws can cost thousands of dollars with inconsistent long-term retention.

Tomislav Peric recognized these systemic issues and built the Feel Tennis platform to provide a structured, highly visual, and logically progressive curriculum that players can study and absorb at their own pace.

Who Is Tomislav Peric?

Before investing in any instructional program, players want to know who is behind the camera. Tomislav Peric is a professional tennis coach, founder of FeelTennis.com, and creator of some of the most popular online tennis training materials available today.

What sets Peric apart from generic YouTube instructors is his coaching philosophy. He focuses heavily on kinesthetic awareness—helping players feel the correct movement patterns rather than just trying to mimic positions visually. His teaching style is calm, analytical, and structured specifically for players who already understand the basics of the game (such as scoring, court positioning, and basic rallying) but want to refine their mechanics, eliminate hitching motions, and gain competitive consistency.

Inside the Feel Tennis Video Instruction Library

The Feel Tennis video library is not a single generic clip; it is a comprehensive suite of specialized masterclasses targeting every major facet of modern tennis stroke mechanics. While individual modules can be selected based on your weaknesses, the core curriculum covers:

1. The Modern Forehand Mastery

The forehand is your primary weapon. The Feel Tennis forehand module breaks down unit turn, racket drop, lag, contact point, and extension into bite-sized visual steps. You learn how to harness kinetic energy from the ground up—using your legs and core rotation—rather than muscling the ball solely with your arm.

2. The Modern Two-Handed (and One-Handed) Backhand

For many players, the backhand is a liability. Peric provides crystal-clear drills that teach you how to lead with the dominant shoulder, maintain proper spacing, and drive through the ball cleanly with confidence, transforming an uncomfortable stroke into a reliable weapon.

3. The Serve Mechanics & Consistency Blueprint

The serve is the only shot in tennis completely under your control, yet it is often the most poorly executed stroke among club players. The course demystifies the trophy position, leg drive, pronation, and rhythm, helping you add effortless power and reliable placement to your first and second serves.

4. Volleys, Approach Shots, and Touch

Modern tennis heavily rewards net play and court aggression. This module teaches concise, compact volley mechanics, footwork adjustment steps, and directional control to help you finish points cleanly at the net.

The Methodology: Why "Feeling" Beats "Thinking"

Many tennis books and video clips fail because they overload the player's working memory with mechanical checklists during a live rally ("Keep your elbow up, turn your shoulders, step forward, watch the ball, snap your wrist!"). By the time you process all those instructions, the ball has already sailed past you.

Peric's unique training philosophy centers around sensory feedback loops. By utilizing specialized shadow-swing drills, slow-motion execution, and progressive resistance exercises off the court (and during practice hitting sessions), the program trains your nervous system to recognize correct movement automatically.

Key pillars of the methodology include:

  • Deconstructing Complex Strokes: Breaking a stroke down into isolated segments so your brain can master one piece at a time before integrating them into a fluid motion.
  • Visualizing Correct Physics: Understanding the exact racquet path and ball contact physics required to generate heavy topspin, slice, or flat drives naturally.
  • Solo and Wall Drills: Providing actionable exercises you can practice even when you don't have a hitting partner available.

How to Maximize Your Results: A 4-Step Practice Blueprint

Buying an instructional course is only half the battle. To truly transform your tennis game using the Feel Tennis framework, follow this proven 4-step integration strategy:

Step 1: Diagnose Your Biggest Weakness

Watch the introductory module and identify the single stroke that breaks down most often under match pressure—whether it's your second serve return, short forehand approach, or backhand consistency. Focus on one module at a time rather than trying to change everything at once.

Step 2: Study and Shadow Swing at Home

Before hitting a single tennis ball, watch the breakdown videos multiple times. Perform shadow swings in front of a mirror at home to build muscle memory and internalize the correct kinetic chain without the distraction of an incoming ball.

Step 3: Take the Drills to the Practice Court

Dedicate a practice session specifically to drilling. Use a ball machine, hitting partner, or practice wall to execute the specific progressions taught in the course at 50% speed, gradually increasing speed as form locks in.

Step 4: Transfer to Match Play

In your next recreational match, consciously let go of mechanical thoughts and trust the new muscle memory you've built. Evaluate your performance after the match and return to the video modules to fine-tune any areas that slipped back into old habits.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

1. Are these courses suitable for tournament and competitive league players?

Yes! In fact, advanced recreational and competitive UTR/USTA league players benefit the most because they already have functional strokes and need precise biomechanical tweaks to gain competitive edge.

2. How are the video courses delivered?

All courses are delivered digitally. Upon purchase, you receive immediate secure login access to stream or download the video modules across all your devices.

3. Can I practice these drills without a hitting partner?

Many of the foundational shadow-swing drills, footwork exercises, and wall drills can be completed entirely on your own without needing a partner.
